thread.title: ‘Google is at Apple’s mercy’ — the trouble in Alphabet’s earnings

author: Victor Reklaitis
title: ‘Google is at Apple’s mercy’ — the trouble in Alphabet’s earnings
text:
Published: Feb 2, 2018 8:44 a.m. ET Share 
Critical information for the U.S. trading day Getty Images A b-school prof explains what “hurts” for Google parent Alphabet. 
By Victor Reklaitis Markets writer 
Yes, the company’s name is Alphabet GOOG, -4.51% GOOGL, -5.19% these days, but it might as well be mud, if you go by what some bears are saying. 
The miss contrasts with the beats by Apple AAPL, -2.04% and Amazon AMZN, +6.26% — and by this morning’s jobs report . 
One longtime worry for investors is that as people switch away from PCs to smartphones, Google has become more dependent on rivals like Apple to serve up its ads. Perhaps such fears have been confirmed, as Alphabet’s traffic acquisition costs, or TAC, came in above forecasts. 
“Google is at Apple’s mercy for search on iPhones, and that hurts because search has moved to mobile devices,” says University of Michigan business school professor Erik Gordon for our call of the day . 
This “increases its cost to acquire the revenue,” Gordon tells the FT , which also flags the CFO’s hints about another TAC attack in the current quarter. 
Alphabet remains a gorilla that is capable of taking many bananas from other members of tech’s half trillion dollar club . And the stock had roared going into last night’s earnings report, gaining 12% for the year as of yesterday’s close, so don’t cry too much over its premarket drop of 4% or so. 
Check out: Google sold at least $2.7 billion worth of hardware during the holidays 
At the same time, Morgan Stanley analysts have cut their Alphabet price target to $1,200 from $1,215, as they note “margin-dilutive investments” and a slowdown in YouTube’s growth. But they also backed their overweight rating, and FactSet indicates that 84% of analyst teams covering the stock say buy it. 
And see: Google’s cloud unit is a $1 billion business, execs say Key market gauges 
Futures for the Dow YMH8, -0.85% , S&P 500 ESH8, -0.63% and Nasdaq-100 NQH8, -0.32% are slumping, putting the blue-chip gauge on track for a drop of more than 200 points. The Dow DJIA, -0.84% , S&P SPX, -0.67% and Nasdaq Composite COMP, -0.51% are all set for weekly drops, with rising bond yields getting much of the blame. The 10-year Treasury yield TMUBMUSD10Y, +1.47% has topped 2.80% and was recently at 2.79%. 
See the Market Snapshot column for the latest action. The chart BAML This BAML gauge says sell. 
A contrarian sell signal for stocks and other risk assets just got triggered, according to the chart above from Bank of America Merrill Lynch strategists. 
BAML’s Bull & Bear Indicator has surged to 8.6 from 7.9, spurred by factors such as record inflows into stocks and bullish bets by hedge funds. 
The bank’s strategists note that their clients would rather just shift around trades (“play rotation”) rather than position for a big reversal, with some saying, “We only just got bullish!”
